_provenance.kinds: The scanner (python_call_kind in generate_necb_8_4_coverage.py) classifies each article= citation call site into exactly two kinds: 'cited' (any call other than audit.warn/audit.warning) and 'warn' (an audit.warn/audit.warning call). It does not separately distinguish 'decision' from 'info' — both fall under 'cited'. This baseline keys by the scanner's own two kinds, not the three-way decision/warning/info vocabulary used to describe the intent.
_provenance.note: Re-baselined 2026-09-16 for D-92 (DF-11 increment A), which replaced the hydronic-pump MECHANISM: the reference pump's head, shaft coefficient and motor efficiency are stated and its power is left autosized, instead of the power being hard-set and the inherited head bent afterwards. That added exactly ONE new citation site per edition — the audit call in _transfer_pump_power that declares the fall back to a physical efficiency split when the proposed pump's own triple implies an efficiency above 100%, citing f'{prefix}.14.(3)' (2020 8.4.4.14.(3), 2025 8.4.5.14.(3)) because an unreadable efficiency is precisely sentence (3)'s "not known". The scanner resolves that literal onto the parent article, so 8.4.4.14 / 8.4.5.14 'cited' each go 3 -> 4 and the total goes 209 -> 211. Nothing was lost: no other (edition, article, kind) count moved, and the deleted _reconcile_pump_head warning carried a ruling= tag but no article=, so it was never a citation site. Superseded note (kept for the chain): generated AFTER renaming compliance.py's local lighting_prefix -> prefix, which made the article= keyword at compliance.py:346 and its warn-branch sibling scanner-visible.
